channel.description: Latest research, archaeology, manuscripts, heritage and cultural news from Hindu Research Portal.

item.title: Unveiling Ancient India's History through Epigraphs
item.description: The Archaeological Survey of India has undertaken a significant project to digitize 67,461 estampages of Indian epigraphs, shedding light on the country's ancient past. Epigraphs, such as the Naneghat Cave inscription, provide valuable insights into the social, political, and cultural context of ancient Indian society. The study of these inscriptions has been facilitated by discoveries and preservation efforts by epigraphists and institutions like the ASI.

item.title: Deciphering Ancient Shaivite Traditions: 5th Century Sanskrit Seal Uncovered
item.description: The Archaeological Survey of India has successfully decoded a 5th century Sanskrit seal, shedding new light on ancient Shaivite traditions and the existence of a Shaiva temple in the mythical Deodarvana. The seal, discovered in present-day Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, features a rare Sanskrit inscription written in Brahmi script. This discovery contributes to a deeper understanding of India's cultural and religious heritage

item.title: Ancient Indian Inscriptions Uncovered in Egypt's Valley of the Kings
item.description: A recent archaeological discovery in the Valley of the Kings has revealed nearly 30 inscriptions in ancient Indian languages, shedding new light on Indian presence in Ancient Egypt. The inscriptions, dated to between the first and third centuries AD, were found across six tombs and are primarily in Tamil-Brahmi, an ancient language connected to modern Tamil. This finding was presented at the International Conference on Tamil Epigraphy in Chennai by researchers from the French School of Asian Studies and the University of Lausanne.

item.title: Toward a Critical Edition of the Laṅkāvatārasūtra: The Significance of the Palm leaf Manuscript
item.description: This article examines a newly discovered and recently published Sanskrit manuscript of the Jayamatiparipṛcchāsūtra (“Inquiry of Jayamati”) and documents its relationship, previously unrecognized, as part of the Śūraṃgama-samādhisūtra (“The Concentration of Heroic Progress”). item.title: Unlocking India's Archival Treasures: National Archives of India's Digital Initiatives
item.description: The National Archives of India has made significant strides in digitizing its vast repository of records, including declassified files relating to Netaji, to facilitate research and public access. The archives' online portal, Abhilekh Patal, provides a comprehensive search platform for scholars and users. The National Archives of India is the largest archival repository in South Asia, housing a diverse range of records and materials

item.title: Comprehensive Encyclopedia of Hinduism Covers Diverse Aspects of the Tradition
item.description: A new encyclopedia on Hinduism provides an in-depth look at various aspects of the tradition, including art, history, language, and literature. The encyclopedia aims to offer a better understanding of Hinduism in a global context. It covers topics such as Hinduism in different regions and its development in Hindu kingdoms and empires.

item.title: Unpacking the Gurukul System: A Cornerstone of Indian Knowledge and Education
item.description: The Gurukul system is an ancient Indian educational model that emphasizes holistic development through a residential teacher-disciple relationship, focusing on self-discipline, ethical values, and critical thinking. This traditional system aims to integrate spiritual, moral, intellectual, and physical growth in students. The Gurukul model has been influential in shaping India's knowledge framework, with a strong emphasis on mentorship and practical life skills.

item.title: Revitalizing Indian Education: Integrating Traditional Knowledge Systems into Modern Learning
item.description: This research proposes a Spiral Pedagogical Model to incorporate Indian Knowledge Systems into education, from early childhood to adult learning, by drawing from the Gurukul system's emphasis on experiential learning and holistic development. The model aims to provide a relational and humanizing approach to education in a digital age. By analyzing existing literature, the study seeks to understand how traditional Indian knowledge systems can be integrated into modern education
